summary: Intro demo of Redwood Console focusing on per-route dashboards, usage analytics and route-level cost decomposition. Customer interested in pilot on hosted then Dedicated; security and SSO/KMS questions surfaced. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot with sample routes; SE to run quick bench and share config suggestions.
transcript:
[00:00] Lina Park: ok so hi everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Lina from Redwood inference, with me is Marco our systems SE, we'll do a quick console walkthrough then leave time for questions.
[00:12] Aisha Khan: hey thanks, excited — want to understand per-route costs, our finance team is pretty sensitive to token churn.
[00:18] Marco Diaz: great, i'll share my screen now, can you all see the console? (brief pause) i think you can, shout if not.
[00:29] Tom Reynolds: yes, can see. small echo on my end.
[00:34] Marco Diaz: cool. first pane is the usage overview, overall tokens, calls, and what we call routes, which are logical API endpoints in your app, we map them automatically if you forward the route id header. so here's Verdigris sandbox data — note this is synthetic.
[00:52] Priya Sinha: how granular is the cost? like can i see per feature, per team?
[00:58] Marco Diaz: yep, token-level breakdown, per-route, per-model, and you can slice by time windows. down here is token breakdown: prompt vs completion, and we show estimated infra cost vs model license cost. these estimates are based on our runtime metrics and the model profile.
[01:20] Lina Park: to add — the estimates are configurable, so finance can override unit costs to match internal chargeback.
[01:27] Aisha Khan: nice. question: what about cache / kv cache effects? our chatbot keeps repeating prefixes.
[01:34] Marco Diaz: good one. we surface cache hit rates per route, and if you enable prefix caching or kv caching — spelled sometimes kv cash in older exports — you'll see a corresponding delta in per-token infra costs. we also provide suggested cache TTL and which routes are high benefit.
[02:00] Tom Reynolds: are these suggestions automated? or just heuristics?
[02:04] Marco Diaz: a mix — heuristics derived from your traffic shape and model selection, plus an optimization pass that suggests batching or quantization. our Optimize module will propose quantization profiles if you want to trade a bit of quality for cost. sometimes the console calls it "Optimizer" in the UI, which is a small labeling mismatch in the export.
[02:30] Aisha Khan: and routing? we have some sensitive routes that must go to private nodes.
[02:35] Marco Diaz: routing policies are first-class. you can set policies by route to go to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private (VPC). we show a routing summary and fallback chain — if Dedicated is saturated it will fallback to a cheaper hosted variant, or a pinned quantized model.
[02:52] Priya Sinha: can you show an example for a single route?
[02:56] Marco Diaz: sure; clicking into route /nlp/intent we see throughput, p99 latency, token distribution, and a cost waterfall: model runtime, infra, network, and optional license. here's a weird sample: last week there was a spike — the console highlights anomalies and attributes to traffic sources.
[03:22] Lina Park: i'll point out the route comparison view — you can pin top routes and compare side-by-side. finance often uses that to see which 10 routes account for 80% of spend.
[03:34] Tom Reynolds: does it map to our SSO identities? we need RBAC at route level.
[03:39] Marco Diaz: yes RBAC is integrated with SSO, roles can be scoped to projects and routes. audit logs show who queried route dashboards and who exported billing reports. we integrate with common SAML providers, okta, azure ad, and you can plug in a customer KMS for key management.
[03:58] Aisha Khan: KMS — do we need to use it for embeddings? our PII redaction pipeline holds vectors in ephemeral storage.
[04:05] Marco Diaz: embeddings can be configured to never leave your VPC if you run Redwood Private. with hosted we encrypt at rest; for extra control you can bring your own key, k-m-s, and we rotate keys per your policy.
[04:21] Priya Sinha: excellent, security team will want the SOC2 docs — can you send those?
[04:25] Lina Park: absolutely, i'll send our security pack and SOC2 report after.
[04:30] Marco Diaz: back to the console, here's the cost model tune page — you can change per-token cost assumptions, and the charts reflow so you can model chargeback scenarios.
[04:43] Tom Reynolds: do we get CSV export? our billing system wants a nightly file.
[04:48] Marco Diaz: yes, there's an exports page and an API endpoint. you can schedule daily exports with granularity by route and model. also a billing reconciliation view for quick diffs.
[05:02] Aisha Khan: about pilot — we were thinking 2 weeks, top 8 routes, sample traffic replay. would that work?
[05:09] Lina Park: yes that's our standard pilot: we run a sandbox and optionally mirror traffic to a dedicated pool for throughput validation. Marco will run a bench and provide latency/cost numbers for 8k and 16k seq.
[05:20] Marco Diaz: i'll include sequence length impact, batching profiles, and an example autoscale policy. one note: the autoscaler is workload-aware, so if you have bursty traffic it keeps a small warm pool and bursts to reserved capacity.
[05:36] Priya Sinha: cost questions — how do we price inter-region traffic?
[05:40] Marco Diaz: we show network egress in the waterfall. you can pin routes to region to avoid cross-region costs, or set a policy to route regionally first.
[05:49] Aisha Khan: curious about model variants — if Dedicated runs out, what fallback do we see?
[05:53] Marco Diaz: fallbacks can be a quantized variant or hosted fallback. you can define SLOs, and if the primary fails we either queue, spill to fallback, or send an error depending on policy. recommended pattern for user-facing routes is a fast low-cost fallback that preserves basic functionality.
[06:12] Tom Reynolds: any integrations with our observability stack? we use datadog and prometheus.
[06:16] Marco Diaz: yes we export metrics, traces, and logs; there are direct integrations and an open telemetry pipeline. you can correlate Redwood traces with your app traces to find hotspots.
[06:28] Aisha Khan: can we tag routes with product teams? e.g., agent-team, search-team.
[06:32] Marco Diaz: yep tags are first class. you can build chargeback by tag and do per-team dashboards.
[06:38] Lina Park: quick demo of a finops workflow — Priya, imagine you want to cap spend on non-prod routes; you can set alerts and an auto-fallback to a cheaper model when threshold is hit.
[06:50] Priya Sinha: neat. what about rollouts, we need canaries for model changes.
[06:55] Marco Diaz: canary rollouts supported, you can route a percentage to the new model and measure quality via evals integrated in console, with automatic rollback if quality regresses. small footnote — some transcriptions call this the "eval pane" or "examiner" but same idea.
[07:12] Tom Reynolds: for the bench, what hardware will you run on? we want numbers on T4 vs A100.
[07:17] Marco Diaz: we'll run on a mix: a dense 4xA100-style cluster for peak throughput and a T4-like baseline. bench spreadsheet will show tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, and p99 latency samples.
[07:31] Aisha Khan: any gotchas with context windows > 8k? our RAG flows often go to 16k.
[07:36] Marco Diaz: yes longer contexts raise memory and latency; console shows expected KV cache hit ratios and we suggest a hybrid approach: prefix caching plus quantized model for long contexts. for high long-window traffic Dedicated with pinned GPU flavors is usually cheaper.
[07:55] Lina Park: quick note on privacy: audit logs and go-to-console access controls let you show compliance to auditors.
[08:02] Priya Sinha: ok, let's talk pricing basics.
[08:06] Lina Park: for hosted we do per-token billing; Dedicated is a committed monthly reserve with predictable throughput — you get a discounted unit cost. we'll tailor pilot pricing.
[08:17] Priya Sinha: is there a hard SLA for latency?
[08:21] Marco Diaz: for Dedicated we offer latency targets and uptime SLAs in the contract. hosted has best-effort but we provide SLO guidance.
[08:30] Tom Reynolds: about data residency — our legal team requires EU data not leave region.
[08:33] Marco Diaz: supported — route-level regional pinning or Private deployment keeps data on-prem.
[08:38] Aisha Khan: earlier you mentioned model catalog — can we pin a model revision?
[08:42] Marco Diaz: yes, version pinning supported and rollouts are per-route. you can also pin quantization profile.
[08:49] Priya Sinha: any hidden fees e.g., export fees?
[08:53] Lina Park: exports are included up to a threshold; large retention or premium export formats can be add-ons. we'll include details in the pricing document.
[09:01] Aisha Khan: can you show the anomaly detection?
[09:04] Marco Diaz: sure — console flagged a cost spike; clicking in shows sample requests and payload size; we even surface if a route had a repeated long prompt due to client bug.
[09:18] Tom Reynolds: we need retention controls — HR asks for 90 day logs only.
[09:22] Marco Diaz: retention is configurable; you can set different retention for telemetry versus request payload. we also have scrubbers for PII before logs leave the host.
[09:34] Lina Park: sounds like we're lining up pilot items — Aisha will send the list of top routes and a sample traffic replay, Marco will run bench, Priya will scope budget.
[09:46] Aisha Khan: yep i will.
[09:48] Priya Sinha: one more question — can we set per-route budget alerts to auto-apply throttles?
[09:53] Marco Diaz: you can set hard limits and soft alerts; hard limits can trigger throttles or divert to a cheaper model.
[09:59] Tom Reynolds: curious if exporting to our billing system preserves tags.
[10:02] Marco Diaz: yes metadata and tags flow through the export.
[10:07] Lina Park: ok quick recap and next steps — i'll share the SOC2 pack, Marco will share bench spreadsheet and recommended config, and we'll schedule kickoff for the pilot once Verdigris shares route list.
[10:21] Aisha Khan: thanks, this was very helpful.
[10:24] Priya Sinha: thanks everyone.
[10:26] Tom Reynolds: thanks.
[10:30] Lina Park: i'll follow up with calendar invites for the pilot kickoff and include a short doc with success criteria.
[10:40] Marco Diaz: leaving an internal note — watch out for one of the console labels that shows up as "Optimizer" in some exports, it's the same as Optimize.
[10:52] Lina Park: ok meeting end.

Note: transcript includes mild transcription artifacts (speaker overlaps, product name mismatches in some auto-exports). Links mentioned: Sandbox URL: https://sandbox.redwood.ai/verdigris (credentials to follow), Bench spreadsheet: https://redwood.ai/bench/CRM-789412 (shared), Security pack: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2.pdf (to be shared).
